summary: Re-tested M2-S02 (access) after its repair pass (metadata-builder, envelope 2026-09-19T15-22-09Z): the org refused the Sales User profile overlay on mock-deploy dry run 1 (N3-F-05, reports/MOCK-DEPLOY-M2.md), so both recordTypeVisibilities blocks were removed from profiles/Sales User.profile-meta.xml (its two layoutAssignments blocks are byte-identical to before), and two fieldPermissions blocks (Discount__c editable, Approval_Status__c read-only) were added to permissionsets/Enterprise_Sales_Record_Types.permissionset-meta.xml, closing HIGH open item O-M2S02-01. The prior tests/M2-S02/results.json (run 2026-09-19T14-39-24Z) was stale because both metadata files' hashes changed; it is overwritten by this run. Ran all three declared checkers verbatim from the build directory at their plan-declared scopes -- check_permission_set_architecture.py and check_record_type_layouts.py at build scope (--manifest-dir artefacts), check_access_model.py at step scope (--manifest-dir artefacts/M2-S02) -- plus the always-on xml parse (3/3 files) and manifest consistency check (package.xml unchanged and still consistent both directions), plus check-outputs --hashes. All five runnable tests passed with the same findings as the pre-repair run: permission-set-architecture 'No issues found.' (PSVP-FLS-01 stays silent -- the set still grants no objectPermissions, so adding fieldPermissions did not create the shape that rule fires on); record-type-layouts at build scope 1 REVIEW RTL-MERGE-01 (pre-adjudicated O-M1S02-03, unaffected by this repair); permission-sets-vs-profiles at step scope 1 WARN PSVP-FLS-02 (accepted by design O-M2S02-02, unaffected -- the profile still carries zero objectPermissions/fieldPermissions after the repair). Both manual acceptance tests remain deferred to the M2 milestone gate, never ticked here; manual test 1's wording is now stale against the repaired artefact (it asserts the profile carries 'two recordTypeVisibilities blocks... every recordTypeVisibilities carries default=false', which the repair removed entirely) and is flagged as unusable-as-worded without being rewritten. results.json rewritten with "passed": true and fresh artefact_hashes from check-outputs --hashes; M2-S02 moved built -> tested via build_plan.py set-status (exit 0; 19 pre-existing WARNs on unrelated steps M1/M3/M4 printed on the full-plan validate pass, none naming M2-S02 or its cited skills).
confidence_rationale: Every declared test ran (or was correctly classified as manual), both always-on checks completed, and every result came from an exit code this agent observed directly -- which would clear the Step 7 HIGH bar on its own. Held to MEDIUM instead because manual test 1's own wording no longer describes the artefact it is checked against (it asserts a recordTypeVisibilities shape the repair deliberately removed), which is a defect in the acceptance-test text this agent can report but not fix -- per agents/step-tester/AGENT.md Step 7's MEDIUM row, this is the same class of finding as a manifest exclusion or a refused command: the artefacts under test are fully covered, but what the test asserts is now incomplete relative to reality.

process_observations.observation: All three declared checkers exited 0 on the repaired artefacts, reproducing the exact same findings as the pre-repair run (permission-set-architecture: 'No issues found.'; record-type-layouts: 1 REVIEW RTL-MERGE-01; permission-sets-vs-profiles: 1 WARN PSVP-FLS-02) -- the repair changed only recordTypeVisibilities in the profile and fieldPermissions in the permission set, and neither checker's finding set moved as a result, which is the expected outcome given what each checker actually inspects.

PSVP-FLS-01 (a permission set granting object CRUD with zero field permissions) stayed silent after the repair added two fieldPermissions blocks to Enterprise_Sales_Record_Types, confirming deploy-order.md section 6.2's own claim that the set still declares no objectPermissions element and so does not create the shape that rule fires on.

evidence.detail: raw JSON output names only PSVP-FLS-02, not PSVP-FLS-01

process_observations.observation: package.xml is byte-identical to the pre-repair run (hash 82dfb95a...606bff unchanged) and remains consistent in both directions after the repair, because the repair changed metadata file content, not file identity or location.

Manual acceptance test 1 (Q4/Q9, on profiles/Sales User.profile-meta.xml) is now stale as worded: its Then clause asserts the profile contains 'two recordTypeVisibilities blocks, every recordTypeVisibilities carries default=false', but the repair removed both recordTypeVisibilities blocks entirely (deploy-order.md section 6.1) to resolve the org's N3-F-05 refusal. The remainder of the Then (no userPermissions/objectPermissions/fieldPermissions/applicationVisibilities/classAccesses in the profile) is still true, and the underlying intent (overlay adds access, revokes nothing) still holds functionally -- visibility now lives solely in the permission set -- but the test's literal wording would fail a human trying to tick it as written. Not rewritten by this agent; carried into skipped_manual[] verbatim with this flag for the M2 gate reviewer and for whoever next amends the step's acceptance-test text.

evidence.detail: plan.json steps[M2-S02].acceptance_tests[4].description vs the current file content (zero recordTypeVisibilities elements)

process_observations.observation: Manual acceptance test 2 (Q19, persona access source) was re-checked against the repaired files and remains usable as worded: it never asserted the permission set carries no field permissions, so the two new fieldPermissions blocks do not contradict it -- reps/managers still reach both record types through the permission set, the sales-ops admin still needs no row in either file, and the manager-versus-rep distinction still appears in neither.

set-status's own full-plan validate pass printed the same 19 pre-existing WARNs about other steps (M1, M3, M4) shipping a cited skill's checker with no declared acceptance test for it, unchanged from the pre-repair run. None name M2-S02 or its cited skills (admin/permission-set-architecture, admin/record-types-and-page-layouts, admin/permission-sets-vs-profiles); they predate this run and are outside this invocation's one-step scope.

evidence.detail: stderr of `build_plan.py set-status ... M2-S02 tested`, 19 WARN lines naming M1-S01, M1-S02, M3-S02, M3-S03, M3-S04, M3-S05, M4-S01, M4-S02, M4-S03, M4-S04
